title: MEPS month-ordered events sharpen health, work, and bill-context selection without identifying recovery
source_unit: MEPS 2024 person records with first office, emergency-room, or inpatient event classified relative to the R4/2 reference-period endpoint month

observations.period: 2024; first emergency-room event before R4/2 endpoint month

denominator.unit: people with a first ER event before the endpoint month; outcome-specific valid denominators vary

observations.method: Classify the first valid event month strictly before the person-specific R4/2 endpoint month and compare R4/2 context fields using PERWT24F and 128 MEPS BRR replicates.
observations.uncertainty: Month ordering is not exact-day ordering; the outcome reference period may overlap the event, and event presence reflects prior need, severity, access, coverage, and selection. No causal or recovery estimate is claimed.
observations.subgroup: People with a first emergency-room event before the endpoint month; no-event comparison is the broad valid-person group without an event in the family.
observations.counterinterpretation: The event may mark pre-existing health or work constraints rather than cause the observed R4/2 context.

observations.period: 2024; first inpatient event before R4/2 endpoint month

denominator.unit: people with a first inpatient event before the endpoint month; outcome-specific valid denominators vary

observations.method: Classify the first valid event month strictly before the person-specific R4/2 endpoint month and compare R4/2 context fields using PERWT24F and 128 MEPS BRR replicates.
observations.uncertainty: Inpatient-event respondents already differ strongly in observed health and work context; this is a selected temporal comparison, not an event effect or recovery estimate.
observations.subgroup: People with a first inpatient event before the endpoint month.
observations.counterinterpretation: Pre-existing illness, age, employment, coverage, access, and event severity can account for the later-looking differences.

observations.period: 2024; first office event before R4/2 endpoint month

denominator.unit: people with a first office event before the endpoint month; outcome-specific valid denominators vary

observations.method: Classify the first valid event month strictly before the person-specific R4/2 endpoint month and compare R4/2 context fields using PERWT24F and 128 MEPS BRR replicates.
observations.uncertainty: The near-equal office bill-problem contrast is a counterexample to a universal event-to-burden gradient; office visits differ in severity, continuity, coverage, and purpose.
observations.subgroup: People with a first office event before the endpoint month.
observations.counterinterpretation: Utilization type and continuity may explain the contrast; event presence does not identify a bill, care choice, alternative, or remedy.

related_sources.claim: The method note defines before, same-month, after, and no-event groups and preserves the timing boundary.
The machine output preserves all event families, group counts, estimates, and standard errors.

boundary: This is a month-ordered descriptive transition layer. It does not identify the triggering need or bill, available alternatives, care delay or foregoing, household adaptation, remedy, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence.
